wiki_acceptance: A gated test asserts body-part damage -> part HP drops -> bleed -> downed/death as ONE PASS line.
assert_steps: init — PawnHealth.parts[] populated with 6 entries via HealthPartsConfig.CreateDefault() fallback
Step 1 — TakeDamage(10, LeftLeg): part.hp drops from 20 to 10 (< initial)
Step 2 — part.bleedRate rises from 0 to 2.5 (= 10 * 0.25f) immediately after TakeDamage
Step 3a — LeftLeg drained to 0 HP; non-vital part at 0 does NOT set IsDead (confirms non-vital semantics)
Step 3b — TakeDamage(25, Head): head.hp reduces to 0 → CheckDeath sets IsDead=true AND IsDowned=true
api_used_read_only: PawnHealth.TakeDamage(int dmg, PartId? preferPart) — existing public combat API, zero edits
PawnHealth.parts[] — public array; BodyPart.hp / bleedRate / maxHp are public fields

api_gaps_flagged_for_qa.description: PawnHealth.parts[], BodyPart.hp, BodyPart.bleedRate are public — read directly without reflection. No gap.
PawnHealth.TakeDamage(int, PartId?) is the existing public combat API. No gap.

PawnHealth [SerializeField] HealthPartsConfig reference is not wired in a headless test scene. PawnHealth.Awake() calls HealthPartsConfig.CreateDefault() when partsConfig is null, creating a runtime ScriptableObject instance with canonical defaults (head 20, torso 40, limbs 18-20). QA should confirm CreateDefault() path executes without error in batchmode.
api_gaps_flagged_for_qa.workaround: No workaround needed; CreateDefault() branch already exists in runtime code.

api_gaps_flagged_for_qa.description: IsDowned for PawnHealth is driven by CheckDeath() (private), which fires synchronously inside TakeDamage. The test reads IsDowned immediately after TakeDamage returns — no frame delay needed. QA should confirm IsDowned is correctly true after head HP reaches 0.

The bleed tick in PawnHealth.Update fires once per real second (Time.time gated). The test reads bleedRate immediately after TakeDamage (before any Update tick fires), so the bleed assertion is frame-deterministic and does not require WaitForSeconds. If batchmode deltaTime is unusual this remains safe because bleedRate is set inside TakeDamage synchronously.

note: Step 3a verifies non-vital part zero-HP semantics (leg at 0 = no death), which strengthens the gate beyond the minimum V6 spec. Step 3b directly asserts the downed/death threshold via head HP=0. bleedRate is read immediately post-TakeDamage (frame-deterministic, no Update tick required).
